game.name: Haste
game.short_description: Run fast, soar through the air, and master your landings as you speed through procedural worlds to outrun the end of the universe, by yourself and with friends!

placements.verbal_evidence: "I prefer it more than cave... I'm even going to put it here." No tier letter spoken.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 5 (2026)
commentary.summary: Haste is a fast-paced 3D running roguelite where you race from the start to a portal while a void chases you, chaining dives and perfect landings to keep energy up for your active ability. He finds it skill-intensive but deeply satisfying once it clicks, with excellent visuals and standout music. The roguelite layer is light but impactful, deliberately so as not to disturb the core movement. Updates since his earlier review fixed many of his complaints. He enjoyed it enough to keep playing well past what the tier list required and places it high on the board, though the exact tier letter is not spoken.
praise: Core movement and dive/perfect-landing system feels great and rewards mastery
Excellent visuals and a large, high-quality soundtrack he listens to outside the game
Roguelite elements (passives, actives, gems) blend well without straying from the core running
Active abilities (board, wings, jump) enable distinct playstyles
Post-launch additions: per-level modifiers, harder modes, better keyword and item explanations
Extremely satisfying and fun; he kept playing beyond what he needed for the ranking
criticism: Losing all health costs a life and restarts the same level layout or boss, which feels tiring
Active abilities are too expensive, discouraging experimentation with builds
Loop mode gives few items, making an endless mode less appealing
Bosses can be frustrating and are hard to make work in a running game
Hub area could use more secrets and things to do; runs do not differ drastically from each other
unique_points: Momentum-and-angle based movement with perfect landings feeding an energy system
Roguelite layer kept intentionally minor to protect the core mechanic
Four biomes repeated at higher intensity with randomized levels
commentary.quote: What you see is what you get.
comparisons: Cave (Cave of Qud-style pick unclear; he says he prefers Haste)
design_criteria: Core gameplay feel: movement and skill ceiling dominate the evaluation
Roguelite integration: elements should support, not disrupt, the core mechanic
Visuals and audio: art and music are major strengths
Meta-progression: stats and unlocks acceptable but active abilities overpriced
Run variety: modest differences between runs, deemed acceptable
Failure/retry design: restarting the level on life loss is tedious
Boss design: uneven, constrained by the running genre
Hub and endgame modes: hub lacks content, loop mode lacks items
Clarity of information: improved keyword and item descriptions
commentary.rerank_note: He reviewed the game previously in a standalone video; since then it has been updated and many earlier issues were fixed, so this is a re-evaluation.

community.one_liner: A third-person, momentum-based 3D parkour/runner roguelite from Landfall in which you play Zoe, sprinting and gliding across procedurally generated levels and chaining perfect landings to outrun a collapsing universe, solo or in online co-op.
community.consensus_summary: Haste is received very positively overall: Steam sits around 92% positive across roughly 14,000 reviews (Very Positive) and Metacritic shows an 81 Metascore from 6 critics with a 7.5 user score from 49 ratings. Nearly everyone, including the people who downvote it, agrees the movement and sense of speed are outstanding, and the soundtrack and art get frequent praise. The recurring complaint is that everything wrapped around the movement (procedural levels, pick-3 item roguelite layer, only three bosses, wordy story) is thin and repetitive, with novelty fading around shard 3-4. It launched on PC on April 1 2025 (a full release, not early access); console versions with crossplay followed later, and a late patch note says the last planned content update has shipped, so future work is ports and bug fixes rather than new content.
best_things: Movement and sense of speed: chaining perfect landings, reading terrain and weaving obstacles feels fluid, tactile and arcade-like; repeatedly compared to what a good 3D Sonic or Tiny Wings in 3D would feel like
Soundtrack: drum-and-bass style tracks with smooth blending between levels are called out by players and by critics (e.g. But Why Tho) as a highlight
Art style and character design are widely described as charming and gorgeous
Skill expression: no jump button, high skill ceiling, and S-rank chasing gives mastery payoff; flow state when it clicks
Late-game and endless-mode item snowballing (RoR2-style) lets runs go absurdly fast, which fans find hilarious and satisfying
Runs great, including 60fps on Steam Deck, and DualSense haptics are praised
Good value and broad appeal: cheap-ish at $19.99, Sonic-fan catharsis, works as a chill or background game
Critics (But Why Tho 9/10, Vandal 82, The Games Machine 80) call it a refined arcade experience
worst_things: Levels are procedurally generated and, per many negative reviews, blur together with mostly palette and obstacle changes across the 10 shards
Only three (some say four) bosses, recycled and made tougher in later shards; the final boss is called underwhelming by some
Roguelite layer is shallow: many items are small stat or condition bonuses, few change how you play, and runs feel similar
Story and dialogue are frequently criticised as wordy, flat or badly paced for a game about going fast; many players skip it
Procedural generation can produce bad terrain or no-win stretches, with obstacle clusters forcing hits and some boss setups depending on luck
Bugs and performance issues reported by some: crashes, freezes, black screen after Continue, stuttering, lag in extreme endless runs
Multiplayer is thin: players share a world but barely interact beyond gifting lives and items, so buying extra copies disappoints some
Repetition after the early shards (novelty wears off around shard 3-4) leads several reviewers to a thumbs-down despite loving the core
improvements: Hand-crafted or curated levels (Clustertruck, Neon White and Cyber Hook are cited as better comparisons), possibly with time-trial and leaderboard support
Items that change playstyle or act as permanent mechanics rather than small stat boosts; more build variety
More bosses and more distinct biomes and level variety per shard
Stronger, better-paced story or an option to skip or trim dialogue; UI readability (speed indicator is easy to miss)
Fixes for procedural-generation edge cases (no-win landings, luck-dependent bosses) plus accessibility options such as a screen shake toggle and the ability to decline challenge rewards
More content or DLC and mod support; players were disappointed the devs said no more content updates are planned
unique_things: Sonic-like speed and momentum fantasy in a roguelite with no jump button; speed is built by timing landings on downslopes
Landing-quality mechanic (perfect, good, bad landings) that drives both speed and score
Sparks economy and item snowballing that can let endless mode reach absurd speeds
Ten-shard campaign with a node map, characters and story wrapped around a runner, plus an endless mode and later time trials
Drop-in online co-op with crossplay on consoles, and a Workshop mod scene (e.g. character swaps)
Built by Landfall (Totally Accurate Battle Simulator, Clustertruck) with a playful tone and Steam Deck-friendly performance
tedious_or_disliked: Shards can run around 20 minutes and feel long and samey once novelty fades
Forced dialogue and story beats between levels; many skip them
Grindy achievements: one reviewer cites the 5000 km achievement as requiring a long endless slog, and shard 10 achievements as annoying
Permanent upgrades (anti-spark and similar) feel like plain stat bumps, and some players need repeated runs for them
Collision or terrain trapping in ditches, unavoidable obstacle clusters, and luck-driven level layouts that can ruin a no-hit attempt
Challenge nodes and the map feel tacked on, and several reviewers say items and map choices can be ignored while still getting S ranks
divisive_points: Whether the roguelite structure belongs: many negative reviewers say a hand-crafted level game would be better, while positive ones say procedural runs and item snowballing drive replayability
Story and characters: some find Zoe and the cast cute and delightful, others find the writing boring and overlong
Difficulty: some call it too easy (items and speed trivialise it) while others hit boss and level-generation spikes they find unfair
Multiplayer: fine as a casual drop-in for some, disappointing as true co-op for others
community.reception_notes: Launched April 1 2025 on PC (Windows, Mac, Linux) and became a strong word-of-mouth hit, boosted by short-form video clips; Steam-based revenue trackers estimate roughly $5.0M gross and 100-200k owners (estimates, not audited). Landfall kept patching for about a year: 1.8 added inventory reordering and Wraith story content (Nov 2025), 1.9 a UI overhaul and cooldown item rebalance (Dec 2025), 1.10 Time Trials (Feb 2026), 1.11 crossplay and console launches on PS5, Xbox and Switch 2 (Apr 2026), then 1.11.b and 1.11.C stability and endless-mode save fixes. The devs said the last planned content update has shipped, and some reviewers are sad about that. Current Steam community threads show scattered bug reports (stuttering, black screen after Continue) and accessibility requests. Steam also lists a demo. Note the Steam listing title is just Haste, and the store page's own copy says ten Shards and 90+ items. OpenCritic score could not be retrieved; web search budget was exhausted so Reddit and OpenCritic were not reached.
